findings.problem: The search box can overwrite what the user typed. Every debounced keystroke calls router.replace, and each navigation commits on its own. The resync effect treats any params.q that differs from the LAST value pushed as an external change, then calls setValue(params.q) and clears the pending timer. When a round-trip takes longer than the pause between keystrokes, the commit for an older value (for example q=t) lands after lastPushed has moved on to 'to' or 'tol'. The input then jumps back and keystrokes are lost. Reproduced against `next start` in headless Chromium, with CDP adding 400–800 ms latency and 350–500 ms pauses between keys. Typing 'tolkien' ended with both the input and the URL reading 'tolin', 'toie' or 'tlin'. It did not reproduce on localhost, where round-trips took 30–60 ms in dev and prod, so it only bites on slow machines or hosted deploys. It breaks the ARCHITECTURE §6.4 promise that typing is never clobbered.
findings.fix: Treat every value this input pushed as its own echo, not just the last one. Keep a ref queue of pushed q values. In the effect, if params.q is in the queue, drop the entries up to and including it and return. Resync only for values that were never pushed (a tab click, 'Clear search', Back). Another option: wrap router.replace in startTransition and skip resyncing while that transition is pending.

findings.problem: After a confirmed delete, Back shows the deleted book as if it still existed. deleteBook deliberately skips revalidatePath (D11), and the client uses router.push('/'), so the detail page stays in history with its cached RSC payload. Reproduced: open Station Eleven from / → Delete → confirm → browser Back. That showed /books/demo-station-eleven with h1 'Station Eleven' and live controls. Changing its status there toasted the generic "Couldn't save changes. Try again.", which is misleading because the book is gone and retrying can't work. A status change, which does revalidate, followed by Back shows fresh data, so the delete path is the only one affected.
findings.fix: Use router.replace('/') instead of router.push('/') in handleConfirm, so the deleted book's detail entry leaves history. In the probe, the earlier '/' entry refetched fresh (0 Station Eleven cards). Optionally, StatusSelect and RatingControl could show result.error when it is 'Book not found' instead of the generic retry message.

findings.problem: The binding architecture contract still describes the two behaviours that round 1 fixed as data-loss bugs. §6.3 (line 504) enables the reset hook when `NODE_ENV !== "production"`, and §9 (line 634) says it is 'always on in dev'. §8 (lines 620–623) says ensureInitialized runs the destructive replaceWithDemoData on first run. The code now correctly gates the hook on E2E_TEST_HOOKS === '1' plus a JSON/Origin check, and seeds without ever deleting. A later fixer or builder who treats ARCHITECTURE.md as the source of truth could 'restore conformance' and bring both bugs back.
findings.fix: Update §6.3, §8 and §9 to match the code. The hook is enabled only when E2E_TEST_HOOKS=1, requires Content-Type application/json, and rejects a foreign Origin with 403. ensureInitialized runs in one transaction that creates the AppSettings marker and inserts the demo rows only when the book table is empty; it never deletes. It is called from every read helper and every mutating action.
